title: Fitting Linear Mixed-Effects models for statistical analysis on PhD project: Urgent help needed
description:
Biostatistics help needed (Urgent) for PhD Study on Cancer Treatment OutcomesAre you a skilled biostatistician with a passion for working with Cancer datasets? I'm urgently seeking an experienced individual to help me analyse my PhD research dataset of Repeated measures (Two time points).**Project Overview:**My PhD study focuses on understanding cancer treatment outcomes using repeated measures data collected at two time points. I need to analyze the data using mixed effects models to uncover insights into the effectiveness of different treatment modalities. I will provide a mock dataset for you to work on, so I can learn the R-code and apply it my dataset, using your help.**Key Responsibilities:**1. Organize Treatment Sequences: My dataset includes information on different treatment types, with the Start +End dates of treatments for each subject. The treatment sequences for each subject need to be organised chronologically .2. Apply mixed effects models to investigate propensity-weighted treatment outcomes.3. Implement Covariance structures to account for correlation between repeated measures.4. Utilize restricted maximum likelihood (REML) methods and associated correction methods for standard error estimation.5. Build covariate-adjusted mixed effects models, adjusting for various demographic and clinical factors.6. Compute and compare outcome measures at different time points and by treatment group.7. Provide step-by-step R code for each analysis step.**Qualifications:**- Master's or Ph.D. in Biostatistics, Statistics, or a related field.
- Experience in analyzing repeated measures data using mixed effects models, preferable in cancer datasets
- Proficiency in statistical software such as R, with the ability to provide R code for each analysis step.
- Familiarity with methods for handling correlated data and mixed models.
- Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively .**Duration and Location:**Due to PhD deadlines I need someone available as soon as possible. The dataset is cleaned and fairly straighforward . I've set a fixed price expecting ~6 hours of work, but this is flexible. There will be opportunities for long-term engagement based on project needs and your performance.**How to Apply:**If you're excited about contributing to cutting-edge research in cancer treatment outcomes and have the expertise to execute complex statistical analyses, I want to hear from you!Please submit your CV, along with a cover letter highlighting your relevant experience and skills.If you have published any research papers ( author/co-author) involving LMM/REML methods, that would be fantastic ! Please send them to me.

So basically, there's always going to be a maximum of two images overlaying each other. First the legs, than the table top on top of that. And then depending on the selected model of the legs, and the color of the legs and table top, one of those images, or both of them need to change while keeping the tabletop image in front always.Although nice to have, It's not necessary to have the option to enlarge the product image or to let it pop-up in a lightbox or something like that.

description:
We are seeking a skilled and experienced developer to create an advanced chatbot using OpenAI's ChatGPT model. The primary function of this chatbot will be to interact with customers on Facebook Messenger, catering to our real estate business. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in AI chatbots, particularly with OpenAI technologies, and experience integrating bots with social media platforms like Facebook Messenger.Key Responsibilities:
- Develop a chatbot using OpenAI's ChatGPT that integrates seamlessly with Facebook Messenger.

If matches are found, the bot will present these options to the user. If no direct matches are available, the bot will ask the user if they are willing to adjust their criteria and present the closest matches.Follow-Up for Future Matches: For users whose criteria cannot be immediately matched, the chatbot will offer to notify them when a matching property becomes available, and automatically send a message once a suitable property is added to the inventory.Scheduling Visits: When a potential tenant expresses interest in an apartment, the chatbot should facilitate scheduling a viewing appointment, propose available dates and times, and confirm the visit.Database Integration: The chatbot must integrate seamlessly with the existing property inventory database to pull real-time information and update the database with information about user inquiries and scheduled visits.User Experience and Interface: The chatbot should provide an intuitive and friendly user interface, with clear instructions and feedback, and handle common queries with helpful responses.Integration with Facebook Messenger API.Development of a backend system for chatbot logic and database management.Use of natural language processing (NLP) techniques.Implementation of a secure method for database updates and queries.Required Skills and Qualifications:
- Proven experience in developing chatbots, specifically with OpenAI's ChatGPT.
- Strong programming skills in relevant languages and frameworks (e.g., Python, JavaScript).
- Experience with Facebook Messenger's API and integration of chatbots on this platform.
- Familiarity with database management and integration for data retrieval purposes.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and spoken. If possibleDesirable Skills:
- Previous work on similar projects in the real estate domain.
- Good understanding of french since most of the customers are french.

title: Expert Go Developer with Real-Time Data Processing and (some) Financial Market Skills
description: API : https://github.com/polygon-io/client-goTo ensure the accuracy and reliability of our system, it is crucial to manage system time effectively, particularly in addressing time drift. This entails continuous synchronization with an NTP (Network Time Protocol) server to maintain alignment with global time standards. Once we know the Timedrift and our latency we can also use timestamps of incoming data to align continuously as the timestamp will be based on the exchange which is very precise.For data acquisition, we leverage both the Polygon API (available via Go or RESTful interfaces). The process is initiated by specifying a target date, for example, [phone removed], to the Go program. Utilizing the API, the system retrieves all option contracts for "O:SPXW" (excluding "SPX" optiosn) expiring on the specified date, with strike prices within a 5% range above and below the current market value.Additionally, the API facilitates querying the last known index price for "I:SPX", providing a reference for market conditions to be able to get that 10% above or below.From the retrieved data, we expect to isolate approximately 100-150 contracts expiring on the given day. Subsequently, the system establishes a connection to the WebSocket for real-time data streaming or utilizes the Go API for the same purpose, encompassing all relevant contracts. utilizing both our system clock and time stamps from incoming data we can move forward in 500ms increments.We begin by aggregating data points every 500 milliseconds, starting at 9:30:00.000, capturing both the first quote and the initial index point of the trading session. It's important to note that we are dealing with real-time quotes, utilizing the last available quote closest to 9:29:59.9999 for our initial data point. Additionally, index data is published every second, allowing us to potentially use these timestamps to monitor and adjust for any clock drift, as they are issued precisely every second.An example of the data format we receive is as follows:"ask_exchange": 302,"ask_price": 9.8,"ask_size": 3,"bid_exchange": 302,"bid_price": 9.4,"bid_size": 1,"sequence_number": 303635,"sip_timestamp": [phone removed]For each of the 100+ contracts, we calculate the midpoint price by averaging the ask_price and bid_price. This value serves as our reference for further calculations. To determine the option's delta, we first need to compute the implied volatility (IV) using a fast bisection method. This calculated IV is then inputted into the Black-Scholes model to compute the delta for each option. I have an example wrote in GO for both of these as guidelines, but might need further optimization.After calculating IV / delta for all options, we organize them to identify those closest to a delta of 0.50 for calls and -0.50 for puts, which indicates options at or near the money.print the put and call option closest to closest abs to .50 delta to terminal showing latency

title: Merge csv files into single excel
description: ========================================Project Title: PowerShell Script for Importing CSV Files into Excel SheetsObjective: The objective of this project is to develop a PowerShell script that imports CSV files into Excel sheets based on specified parameters. The script should be able to handle numbered subdirectories, locate template Excel files, read corresponding map files, and print all parameters before execution.========================================Scope:The script will be developed using PowerShell scripting language.The script will accept a directory path as a parameter, representing the base directory where the operation will be performed.The script will loop through all numbered subdirectories (1,2,3,...) within the base directory.Within each subdirectory, the script will locate all CSV files and corresponding map files.Map files will be in the format of ".csv file name.map" and will contain two columns: XLS_SHEET and XLS_LINE.The script will locate the template Excel file (template.xlsx or template.xls) in a template directory, which is a subdirectory of the base directory.If multiple template files are found, the script will prioritize template.xlsx over template.xls.The script will copy the selected template file into each numbered subdirectory for subsequent operations.CSV files will be imported into different Excel sheets within the template file.Excel sheet names will be defined by the XLS_SHEET column in the corresponding map file.CSV files will be imported starting from the line specified in the XLS_LINE column of the map file.Before executing the import operation, the script will print all parameters for validation and debugging purposes.========================================Out of Scope:The script will not handle exceptions such as missing files or incorrect file formats beyond basic validation.The script will not perform any data validation or transformation on the imported data.The script will not modify the original CSV files or template Excel files.========================================Assumptions:The base directory provided as a parameter will contain numbered subdirectories.Each numbered subdirectory will contain CSV files and corresponding map files.Template Excel files will be located in a subdirectory named "template" within the base directory.CSV files and map files will have consistent naming conventions and formats.The script will be executed in a PowerShell environment where the ImportExcel module is installed and available.========================================Deliverables:PowerShell script file (import-csv-to-excel.ps1) implementing the specified functionality.Documentation including a scope document, usage instructions, and any additional notes deemed necessary.========================================Dependencies:PowerShell environment with access to the ImportExcel module.Proper permissions to read and write files within the specified directories.========================================Attachment are examples of 2 files

title: Modify Management Module Enhancement Odoo 11 community
description:
I need an experienced software developer who can modify and enhance our current shrinkage module, pivoting its functionality for better surplus management.Manufacturing Module WorkflowSelect the desired product to manufacture.Set the quantity to be produced and save the order.Verify the availability of the product for manufacturing.Record the total production.If there is a loss, record the loss.Validate the production order.Changes to be made to the module:Add a button for surplus registration.Surplus: The final production exceeds expectations.Loss: The final production does not meet expectations.The functionality of the button will be the opposite of the loss. When there is a surplus, it should increase the quantity of the final product produced by updating the production yield without affecting the quantities of materials used.*Add a button next to the loss button.Main Requirements:
- Enable us to input the possibility of quantities exceeding 100% in production, meaning if we aim for 100 units and use 100% of the material, it turns out we manage to produce 105, allowing these 5 extra to be entered.-We need to apply an adjustment to our module in order to take control of the surplus. Currently, our system allows us to calculate a shrinkage of finished products. This means that while the material is consumed 100%, it does not manage to produce 100% of the final product due to defects or waste; instead, it only produces 80%. This allows us to close the production process and for the system to accept these differences. We need to apply this in reverse, that is, to use 100% of the raw material but in this case, to produce more than 100% of the finished product.-We can use the same shrinkage workflow, simply reversing it, so to speak. The button should appear as "Surplus" alongside the shrinkage button.Current Scenario: We use a combination of manual and automated tracking to measure production levels.Expected Improvements: We expect important upgrades in our tracking process. The key improvement sought is real-time updating of production levels, offering live updates to manage surpluses effectively at any given moment.Ideal skill set for this project:
- Experience with software development odoo 11- Expertise in automated tracking solutions
- Good understanding of production management systems in odoo 11- Experience with real-time data integration.

- Proficiency in PostgreSQL and experience with other database solutions and their trade-offs.

- Familiarity with event tracking and analytics platforms, preferably Segment and Looker Studio.
- Strong background in data infrastructure design and optimization.# Expectations:
- Deliver a strategic plan outlining recommendations for system improvements, including, but not limited to, alternative data flow methodologies, database technologies, and toolsets.
- Provide a roadmap for implementing proposed solutions, including estimated timelines and potential impact on current operations.
- Offer guidance on best practices for data management and analytics integration.# Working with Us:We value clear communication and are looking for someone who can work closely with our in-house team to understand our current setup and propose effective solutions. We are open to innovative ideas and are looking for a consultant who can guide us through the optimization process with clarity and expertise.

title: IT архитектурная консультация по приложению на aws
description: нужна разовая (пока) консультация по улучшению работы приложения.ситуация такая - работает приложение из нескольких серверов(одинаковых) параллельно. на них с одной стороны приходят внешние уведомления(вебхуки). все уведомления содержат уникальный ID. иногда эти входящие уведомления задваиваются. наше приложение с серверов должно отправить свое исходящее уведомление(вебхук), но только одно, даже если входящие задвоились. сейчас это решается так, что все отправленные уведомления с ID пишутся в бд mysql и если уведомление c ID уже отправлено(проверяется в БД), то не отправляем второй раз. это работает почти всегда, 99.9% времени. проблема возникает в ситуации, если входящие уведомления приходят 2-3 одновременно(миллисекунды) с одним ID. Каждое уведомление проверяется в БД, там ещё ничего нет(и запись в mysql не мгновенная), и отправляется исходящее уведомление, получается что тоже 2-3 раза. как сделать, чтобы проверка существования уведомления была точнее? т.е. если пришло уведомление, быстрее чем сейчас запомнить его ID и другие серверы бы не отправили исходящие уведомления повторно для такого ID?наверняка есть какой-то стандартный способ решения...например, проверить в бд, подождать 1 сек и ещё раз проверить.или запустить условный redis и там все ID сохранять для быстрой проверки.или ещё какой вариант.желательно вариант требующий меньше работы по подключению.хостинг на aws, может там что-то готовое есть.

Once developed, I will provide the necessary data. I have attached a copy of where i at at the moment. I have managed to get to the stage where it is successfully taking the shortest best before product first but if the quantity out exceeds the quantity remaining per items code/batch it doesnt know to take the remainder from the next line with the shortest best before. Reliability is ensured through built-in redundancy, backup mechanisms, and regular maintenance to proactively address potential issues.The system's architecture is structured around a relational database to optimize data storage and retrieval, with a modular and scalable application architecture utilizing a combination of frontend and backend technologies. The user interface design prioritizes user-friendliness and responsiveness, providing intuitive navigation and clear layouts for managing profiles and monitoring digital card balances.Legal and compliance considerations include adherence to requirements for handling personal data and compliance with Section 8 regulations governing housing programs, ensuring data retention policies are established to align with program requirements. title: Software for building maintenance
description:
Design Document for Maintenance Management Software1. IntroductionThis design document outlines the proposed software that will aid in streamlining maintenance tasks, particularly focusing on employee time tracking, material purchases, cost estimation, and comparison, as well as building and HVAC maintenance management.2. System OverviewThe software will be designed to be a comprehensive tool for facility managers and maintenance teams. Its user interface (UI) will be intuitive and user-friendly, ensuring that even those with minimal technical skills can navigate it seamlessly.3. Functional Requirements3.1 Employee Time Tracking:
- Ability to log hours manually or through a digital timer.
- User profiles for each employee with their assigned tasks and hours worked.
- Dashboard to review individual and team hours.
- Reports generation noting hours spent per task and project.3.2 Material Purchases:
- A module to enter purchase information, including material type, quantity, price, and vendor.
- Track the status of the delivery of materials.
- Integration with inventory management to automatically update stock levels.
- Financial reports that reflect material costs per job.3.3 Cost Estimation:
- Interactive tool to input job specifics and calculate estimated costs.
- Template-based estimations for regular maintenance tasks.
- Option to include variable costs such as emergency expenses.
- Historic data analysis to provide more accurate estimations based on past jobs.3.4 Cost Comparison:
- Functionality to input actual costs upon job completion.
- Comparison reports which highlight variances between estimated and actual costs.
- Visual analytics (graphs, pie charts) showing cost breakdowns.
- Recommendations engine for cost-saving measures based on the comparison data.3.5 Building and Unit Management:
- Database to store information on buildings and units including size, location, and type of maintenance required.
- Calendar-based scheduling tool for regular and ad hoc maintenance tasks.
- Notifications for approaching maintenance dates or overdue tasks.
- Facility to document maintenance history for each unit.3.6 HVAC Maintenance Tracking:
- Sub-module specifically for tracking HVAC system checks and maintenance.
- Date tracking for last and next maintenance requirements.
- Alert system for upcoming HVAC maintenance jobs.
- HVAC system lifecycle tracking for predictive maintenance forecasting.Absolutely, automatic billing can be an essential feature for streamlining the financial operations aspect of the software. I will add this feature to the design document under a new section, considering it is related to the financial management aspect of the software.4. Non-Functional Requirements4.1 Security:
- Role-based access controls.
- Encrypted data storage and transfers.
- Regular security audits and compliance checks.4.2 Performance:
- The system should support concurrent use by multiple users without significant performance degradation.
- High uptime availability targeted at 99.9%.4.3 Scalability:
- The system should be capable of expanding to handle more data and users as the organization grows.5. System Architecture5.1 Frontend:
- Built with a responsive design framework for access on desktop, tablet, and mobile.
- Interactive UI components made with a modern JavaScript framework like React or Vue.js.5.2 Backend:
- RESTful API service layer to handle requests and responses between the frontend and database.
- Server-side logic written in a language like Python or Node.js for maintainability and ease of integration.5.3 Database:
- Relational database like PostgreSQL or a NoSQL database like MongoDB, depending on the complexity and structure of data.5.4 Third-Party Integrations:
- Integration with calendar applications (Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook).
- Accounting software integration for financial management and reporting.

title: Modifying & Updating a custom WordPress Plugin to PHP 8 Compatibility
description: Hi,We had a custom WordPress Plugin created before and it's worked solidly so far but we need to make some changes to it.1. The plugin needs to be updated to be PHP 8 compatible.2. The plugin has a shortcode that works correctly, but has an issue with caching causing it to show in the page when it shouldn't.The way it was originally designed was that the PHP generated HTML from the shortcode is ONLY visible when javascript is disabled with no script tags but this isn't happening when the page gets cached resulting it showing on devices where javascript is enabled.The issue is to do with LiteSpeed Cache / Other Caching plugins. We do not want to disable caching on this page. The attempted fix we tried to implement before was using LiteSpeeds Vary Cache. but that never worked.The whole reason we need this is to provide some content for search engine crawlers to be able to get some content.3. The plugin has a function to ping google asking them to crawl the sitemap, it was setup incorrectly but also now Google has discontinued this feature so we are wanting to remove this from the code, but make sure the sitemap data we're providing to WordPress contains the correct LastMod element so crawlers know when it was last modified.4. We need a change so if an item is retrieved in an API response and then later is no longer found in an API response that it doesn't delete the temporary wordpress post but simply hides/unpublishes it.This is because we want a setting added for "Unpublish Expired Items" which should be enabled by default. If enabled then for crawlers/humans the pages would all act identically to they do now however if it's disabled then expired items wouldn't be deleted but instead updated to have a "This item is expired, please visit xxxxx"5. We need simple a user interface created that would list all of the currently retrieved items from the API. It should show the date & time of when they were first retrieved and have a button on the right hand side to "Unpublish" and "Republish" them allowing more control of what goes into the sitemap. If a user changes one of these it would override the "Unpublish Expired Items" feature mentioned in #46. The plugin also needs a button to manually trigger the plugin to check the API for new items.

We look forward to reviewing your application and discussing this exciting project further.

Results in 10-15 different LoRA filesValidation Part 1:Rigorous Testing and validation of the results of the first round of training.Refinement /Re-training:Subsequent training of SDXL LoRA based on the results from Initial Training. Results in 5-10 LoRA files.Validation Part 2:Rigorous testing and validation of the results of the 2nd round of training.DELIVERABLES:Stable Diffusion XL LoRA: A single Fine-Tuned SDXL LoRa checkpoint Model based on the SDXL Base+Refiner workflow, optimized for illustrated and digital styles. (Photorealism is not guaranteed.)ComfyUI Configs: A config file for ComfyUI or StableSwarm that can be used to reliably generate Vambie Images using SDXL on a sufficiently powerful GPU (Minimum 12 GBs vRam). Reliability, in this context, means 1 out of 6 images are correct. The config will include a prompt loader - consisting of appended strings attached to user-generated prompts, processed by Chat GPT to be consumable by Stable Diffusion, thus displaying different images per sentence.Regularization Dataset: Once successful, this dataset can be used for subsequent training. This is meant to be a starting point. Additional adjustments will be needed for subsequent Vambie baby models.Development of Storybook Generator: Users will provide a lesson, starting with specific prompts such as "I want to teach...". The generator will craft a script/story centered around Baby Vambie. Upon user approval, this will be sent to Stable Diffusion for scene generation, culminating in a storybook of no more than 20 pages. If a user decides that a photo is not suitable, they can regenerate the specific image, thus displaying 6 different photos from which the user can choose.Email Delivery of Storybook: Upon completion, users will receive an email containing a URL to their personalized storybook hosted on a specific webpage, along with a downloadable PDF version.Integration with Stable Diffusion: Seamless integration to ensure Stable Diffusion can generate scenes from the created scripts, including a mechanism for regenerating and selecting images for each page as needed. The hosting solution will be provided to ensure availability for a team to generate images for the storybook.Feedback Mechanism & Image Selection Feature: Users will have a feature allowing them to provide feedback on the generated Baby Vambie storybooks. Moreover, they can select from a set of generated images for inclusion in their storybook, with the option to regenerate specific images for better selection.Re-Training Data based on Images Selected: Users who have selected individual images will create a re-training dataset that will let the model learn.User Testing and Refinement: The Contractor will guide at least 3 different individuals through the storybook generation process, making necessary adjustments based on feedback.SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- Stable Diffusion recognizes Baby Vambie with an accuracy rate of 95%.
- Generation of storybooks that align with user-provided lessons, achieving an 80% satisfaction rate amongst parents during internal tests.
- Stories resonate with the Vambie brand, emphasizing spiritual and emotional growth.
- Running three tests involving a minimum of 10 unique parents, with 80% expressing satisfaction with the output.PROJECT TIMELINE:- 2-3 weeks: Stable Diffusion's accurate identification and integration with the Baby Vambie character.
- Within 4 weeks: Stable Diffusion to produce storybooks with Baby Vambie as the hero.

title: Simple Tableau Data Analysis
description: ACME, home of the ACME Kleen Earth Office Shears, is a chain of stores with locations around the world. The dataset contained here includes orders, returns, and customer information.We will use these data for our Data Analytics exercises. The data (Excel) can be found in the attachment. You can register in Tableau for free. Register today as sometimes verification process might take longer than what is expected.Work instructionsCustomer Categorization: The concept began in B2B marketing long ago, and, like Relationship Marketing, has also been adopted by B2C marketing. This idea is simple and closely related to inventory management control. Customers come in three types, A, B and C.‘A’ customers are your most profitable. According to the Pareto Principle, 20% of your customers account for 80% of your profit. These customers deserve your attention and priority. Keep them coming back.‘C’ customers may not be profitable at all or account for very little profit. They’re probably not worth the effort put into them and can be dropped or dissuaded from returning. At the very least, ignore them.‘B’ customers are somewhere in the middle. The aggregate of their sales is large but their profitability is nowhere near ‘A’ customers. Can they be turned into ‘A’ customers? Are they worth that effort?If you’re interested in learning more about customer categorization and profit try this (optional) Harvard Business Review article:This job entails, you guessed it, categorizing Acme’s customers. Identify A, B, and C customers in your assigned Segment (each customer will belong to one of three “buckets”).Analyze the Corporate segment.Build a Story (in Tableau) to show the 3 groups and visually show their profitability (hint: this requires more than just a list of names, but make sure the names are there). (Hint: Tableau wants to cut off the list and you're going to have to do some manipulation to get the top 20 to show properly.) (Note: It's a lot more interesting if you use the bottom of the C customer list rather than the top but it's your choice as to which to show.)Then, go at least one level deeper into the analysis. (This entails figuring out what kind of analysis would be useful as well as performing it.)Your deliverableYou must complete the assignment in Tableau. Then, you will submit a Word document that includes:The Story (create in Tableau; paste into Word) Include evidence that you created the categories; show your customer names (top 20 in each category).What additional analysis did you do? At least two additional analysis you need to conduct.What marketing tactics should be used for each group? (Be specific to your segment.)What would be your next steps in analysis to dig even deeper? only describe what you would do next. No need for actually doing it in Tableau.To help you familiarize yourself with this software, you can watch the following video tutorials:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hr5IE0qYkRshttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jj6-0cvcNEAhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fO7g0pnWaRAPlease note: some of these links are two-hour long videos.

title: Custom Momentum Stock Scanner
description:
I’m looking to develop a custom day trading momentum stock scanner.It revolves around immediate volatility of a stock based on multiples of its previous volatility.I want to use ATR% as the main source of calculations for the scanner.I want to be able to scan stocks based on their recent moves being a multiple of their previous ATR%.ATR% = ATR divided by price, in percentage.example: if a stock’s ATR is 4.01 and the stock price is 50.42, it’s ATR% is 7.95%I want to be able to change the timeframe of the scanner. Initially, it should be for the 5 minute chart, but I want to be able to choose whatever timeframe.Example:Let's say a stock has an ATR% of 2% in its past n candles (for example, 50 candles)I need to be able to choose the value for n.That means the stock has moved un and down within 2% of its share price for the past 50 candles.Then, the stock has a breakout, and the past x candles (for example, 10 candles) have an ATR% of 6%.That’s a 3 time multiple of their previous ATR%.That means the stock is now in a phase where it moved within 6% of its share price for the past 10 candles.I want to filter any stocks that move in a multiple higher than Z times their previous ATR%. I want to be able to choose the value for Z.That’s for the calculation. There’s also more that I want to include:I also want to be able to set the minimum $ volume traded in the past y candles (for example, minimum 10 million USD volume in the past 10 candles)To do the $ volume we’ll do share volume x share price.I also want to be able to have automatically a “liquidity cap” displayed with each stock that will pop in the scanner. The liquidity cap means 1/10th of the average volume of the past y candles (for example, if the stock traded an average of 1 million USD in each of the last 10 candles, the liquidity cap should show 100K USD)I must be able to choose the liquidity cap range (1/10th, 1/100th, 1/50th, etc).The stock scanner must work with premarket data, live data and post market data.

Only stocks traded in NASDAQ, NYSE and OTC.I would like the scanner to run in a private environment (Hosted in the cloud? I’m not an expert in these fields at all) or within a desktop app.Please reply if you are able to do it and let me know how you’re going to proceed. 
I would like a turnkey product with nothing needed other than choosing my inputs. 

Thank you!!

title: BI Analyst / Developer using Lookerstudio and Bigquery
description:
We are looking for a business intelligence analyst that can support our team remotely and expand the current BI landscape that is already in place.To select the right candidate we have created a technical challenge designed to assess your skills in Business Intelligence, specifically focusing on analyzing application usage data. This challenge aims to simulate a real-world scenario where you'll be tasked with extracting insights from application usage data to inform business decisions. You will be using Google BigQuery for data analysis and Google Looker Studio for data visualization. This is an opportunity to showcase your ability to work with complex datasets, your analytical thinking, and your proficiency in creating compelling data visualizations.Objective:Your goal is to analyze a dataset representing user interactions with a web application, focusing on user engagement, feature usage, and retention. Using the Google Analytics Sample Dataset for BigQuery, you will derive insights into how users interact with the application, identify patterns, and visualize these insights in a dashboard using Google Looker Studio.Step 1: Data Analysis in BigQuery:- **Dataset:** `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample`- **Tasks:**1. **Calculate Engagement Metrics:** Determine Daily Active Users (DAU) and Monthly Active Users (MAU).2. **Feature Analysis:** Identify the most and least used features by querying event data.3. **Demographic and Cohort Analysis:** Join user demographic information with session data to analyze usage patterns. Perform a cohort analysis based on user signup date to study retention.4. **Advanced Analysis:** Incorporate session duration and time-of-day analysis to explore when users are most active.Step 2: Visualization in Google Looker Studio:- **Objective:** Create a dashboard in Google Looker Studio that clearly presents your findings from BigQuery, including:1. **Engagement Trends:** Visualize DAU and MAU over time.2. **Feature Popularity:** Chart showing feature usage frequency.3. **User Demographics:** Insights into user engagement segmented by demographics.4. **Cohort Retention:** Visualization of retention rates for different cohorts.5. **Interactive Elements:** Ensure the dashboard includes filters or interactive elements for a deeper data dive.Evaluation Criteria:- **SQL Proficiency:** Complexity and efficiency of SQL queries.- **Analytical Skills:** Ability to extract meaningful insights from complex data.- **Visualization Expertise:** Clarity and effectiveness of the dashboard in communicating insights.- **Data Storytelling:** Competence in narrating a data-driven story that supports business decisions.Dataset Access:
- Access the dataset directly in Google Cloud's BigQuery under `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample`.
- Use standard SQL in the BigQuery console for analysis.Submission Requirements:
- Provide SQL queries used for the analysis.
- Share a link to the Looker Studio dashboard.

Can you discuss your experience with PHP development and working on custom-built applications?2. How would you approach updating the authentication mechanism in the PHP application to align with Firebase's HTTPv1 requirements?3. What testing methodologies do you typically employ to ensure the functionality and reliability of applications post-migration?4. What is your experience with Firebase APIs, and can you provide an example of how you've utilized them in previous projects?5. Can you provide an example of a challenge you encountered while working with Firebase APIs in a previous project and how you addressed it?These questions aim to evaluate the candidate's technical proficiency, problem-solving skills, and familiarity with Firebase, ensuring they are well-equipped to handle the requirements of the migration project effectively.Please Note: Apps using deprecated FCM legacy APIs for HTTP and XMPP must migrate to HTTP v1 API soon. A certification is earned when I particular set of forms is approved by admins. (here, a "form" is like a long paper form consisting of many questions).Some certifications have forms that must be done in order, some can be done in parallel.Admins provide feedback/comments on submitted forms and refer them back to clients. The comments are added to each question in the form.Clients revise forms until they are accepted.Once all required forms are accepted, the certification is earned.A PDF is created from the final certification forms as a record.Forms have text boxes, text areas, checkboxes, radio buttons, and tables.The questions on the form have multiple parts. For example, one question might have two text areas, an array of checkboxes, a set of radio buttons, and a table (tabular data such as lists of contacts).Tables can have a fixed number of rows. Cells should be able to contain sets of controls (e.g. radio buttons) as well as textboxes.Not a lot of form logic, though some textboxes are sums of others. Some validation.A web app is used by clients to manage their side of this.They log in with SSO from Neon CRMThey can see certifications earned, expirations, etc.They can see certifications in process and which forms have been started/revised/approved.They can start a new certificationApp should be responsive so it can be used across multiple device sizesQuestions:
- Is PowerApps a good platform for this?â—‹ Power Pages for client-facing part?â—‹ Automate for workflow and notifications?â—‹ Dataverse for data?â—‹ PowerApps or PowerPages for admin functions? If PowerApps, canvas or model-driven?â—‹ Will maintenance be easier vs. an asp.net solution? Easier to modify forms/schema/workflow, potentially without developer assistance?
- Integration with CRMâ—‹ Want to authenticate with NeonCRM with SSO and access client info from there with little or no replication in the app.â—‹ Neon does OAuth2. PowerPages requires OIDC. Best practices for setting up SSO?â—‹ Best practice for linking together customer data in CRM and authenticated user data in Dataverse?
- Formsâ—‹ Best way to design forms and create schema? Forms are currently paper.â—‹ Best way to organize data given it is hierarchical (e.g. forms, questions, tables)? I've made some progress here with a table for the form, tables for use in subgrids as part of questions, a form per question, and multistep form pages. Have not connected schema to users, organizations, workflows, multi-form certifications, etc. yet.

title:
Need help with building a growth forecast model for the outbound
channel using Google sheets
description:
Outbound has grown to be our #1 revenue driver at our startup and we must model it right. We identified companies in our TAM and the right contacts to contact via email. We send them highly personalized sequences with the goal of generating demos.Based on the following assumptions, this case study aims to build a model to predict the New ARR per month generated from the outbound channel.We need to answer the following questions:
- How many demos can we generate with Outbound?
- How much can we expect to close from Outbound?Expected output: model in casual
- Number of demos booked from Outbound per month
- New ARR closed from Outbound per monthAssumptions
- Outbound channel start date: Jan 2024- Total companies in the TAM: 100,000- Full email volume capacity per month: 120,000- Minimum number of contacts to email per company: 3- Number of emails per sequence: 4- Unsubscribe rate: 1% by sequence(Hint: start by calculating how many companies you can touch per month with your email volume capacity)Total number of sequences before giving up on a company: 4- Cumulative interest rate after these four sequences:(A sequence is sent to a company every two months)
- Month 0: 2%- Month 2: 4%- Month 4: 6%- Month 6: 8%Hint: based on your first cohort of companies first emailed, model the volume of companies touched at sequence #2, #3, and #4 - with their appropriate incremental interest rate to get the total volume of demos per month)
- Close rate: 20% (intra-month closing)
- Deal Size: $10KDefinition:
- Interest rate = Company booking a demo / Company touched via email - Cumulative interest rate: This means if I email 100 companies inJanuary, two will book a demo in January, another two will book a demo in March, another two in May, and another two in July - 7 months after, 8 out of this 100 companies will have secured a demo
- Close rate = Company subscribing to Polar Analytics / Company booking a demo
- Sequence = Suite of 4 emails to be sent to a company in a given month.
- Email volume capacity = How many emails can we send in a given month
- Outbound channel start date = The month where we will contact the firstcompanies for their first sequenceNote : I would need the output with Growth model in casual (https://www.causal.app/)

title: Text Messaging Alert System Facelift
description:
Hi there! I'm part of The SOAR Initiative, a non-profit out of Columbus, OH that aims to prevent overdose deaths throughout the state through technology and innovation. Please see below for the job description, and pay special attention to the note at the end.--Back in ~2019, our Bad Batch Alerts System was created by college students to serve as a pilot text message alert system where Ohioans can submit and receive reports specific to their region within the state about drug lacings, adulterants, unintended side effects, and overdoses. This alert system has grown through the years and we are experiencing system crashes and inconsistencies in retrieving accurate data about the deliverability of these alerts. Additionally, we believe our current system is no longer able to accommodate the number of subscribers we have for the system, let alone handle more users being added. The pilot version of the system, to my understanding, has gone relatively unaltered through the years and has been heavily utilized to get us to where it's at today.Through consulting with a developer, we have been informed that the code that created this alert system was poorly made and inefficient. They have recommended that to fix the current issues, it would be best to hire someone to re-create the system so it's better set up for longevity and growth, rather than having someone tweak the code.In addition, we have many changes we would like to add on to the system including the expansion of text prompts when users are submitting reports about substances they're encountering, to allow for more accurate sharing of information.We are hoping to bring an expert on board who can work independently and bring forth a new and improved version of our Bad Batch Alerts System so we can continue serving our community and preventing deaths. We hope this person can be proficient at explaining their work in layman's terms to us to understand how we can help clarify what we'd like to see happen and understand where the project is at on a regular basis.--With all of this being said, we would like to transparently communicate to you that this job does NOT YET have funding. We are making this job post to serve several purposes:
- We hope to message back and forth with several of you to put together a general timeline for this task
- Once we have a general timeline, we would like to get input on a general cost as well
- Lastly, we'd like to find a candidate who we can hire ONCE we have secured the funds to start the project.

description: Looking for someone who can write a script to scrape all 3000+ US Counties on Redfin on a weekly basis to see active listings vs sold listings (1 month, 3 month, 6 month, 1 year time frames)I use Redfin extensively. The process I use to analyze demand in a market is the following:I choose a county in a state, say cullman county, AL. I then filter for listings 5 acres or more. I then see how many listings are currently available for sale and take note of that number - can call it (Total Active Sales Listing). Then I filter the view to show "Last 1 Month Sold", taking note of that (1 month Sold). Then I filter to "Last 3 Months Sold" (3 months sold). Then filter to "Last 6 Months Sold" (6 months sold). Then "Last 1 Year Sold" ( 1 year sold). I then take each value and divide by the (Total Active Sales) to find the Sell Through Rate for each time period so for instance - the 1 Month Sell Through Rate = (1 month Sold) / (Total Active Sales Listings). I would like to be able to pull this rate each week for all 3000+ counties in the US so that I can gauge demand.

title: Backend for IoT devices with simple web portal
description: We require a back-end implementation for a simple IoT device that will be uploading JSON data for position and some other metadata. We would like to use access keys for authentication, where each device is assigned an ID and a key, securely stored in the device and transmitted as part of the JSON string.The connections will always be via cellular and HTTPS is preferred. We would prefer not to have to use X509 and client certificates. Approximately one packet per hour will be transmitted from each device, and there will be initially only a few devices, expanding eventually to around 1000 maximum.The choice of back-end is up to the developer, we have an Azure instance already but are not averse to creating a subscription with another provider if it will save on costs.The data shall be stored in a database, again it is down to the developer to recommend specific implementation however we are looking for a cost effective solution and performance is not paramount.The web portal shall initially be a very simple maintenance and commissioning page that can be used by the manufacturer of the IoT devices to load them with the keys.As devices are deployed into the field, a desirable function of the website would be to have a login page where registered users (users will be created by the system administrator using the administrative page used to commission devices) can log in using a pre-created set of credentials and view some details pertaining to a single device, presented in a form to be determined but could include a photo of the device and some other details, including the latest data sent from the device itsself. Some of the data is geolocation, and a desirable goal would be to have a map that can show the last uploaded location.We would like to define the API and the server used (and therefore the endpoint addresses and key format) fairly quickly as the first prototype devices are going to be in the hands of testers in the next couple of weeks. We do not need the website operational in this time, but we need to finalise the device firmware for the first device.

title: Build a Shopify public app using Shopify Polaris, Remix and Prisma Database
description: Project Overview:We are seeking a skilled developer to create a Shopify Public App that automates the addition of deposit fees to products in a Shopify store, with a strong emphasis on localization. This app will enable store owners to assign specific deposit amounts to individual products, ensuring that when these products are added to the cart, the corresponding deposit fee is automatically included. This system aims to streamline the process of managing deposits for products such as beverage containers, where a deposit fee is required. The app must be designed to be easily translatable into all languages to accommodate store owners and customers worldwide.Key Features:Deposit Management Settings Page:A user-friendly interface for store owners to create and manage deposit amounts.Ability to define deposit names and corresponding deposit amounts.The interface should be designed to support localization, allowing translations into multiple languages for global usability.Product Selection for Deposits:A dedicated page for selecting products to assign specific deposit amounts.Capability to link different deposit amounts to different products, e.g., $0.10 for beer bottles, $0.30 for wine bottles, etc.Support for localization in product selection and deposit assignment interfaces.Cart Update Logic:Automatic update of the shopping cart to include the deposit fee when a product with an assigned deposit is added.The deposit quantity should match the quantity of the associated product added to the cart (e.g., adding three beer bottles adds three $0.10 deposits).Upon removal of a product from the cart, the corresponding deposit line item should also be removed.Cart updates and messages should be translatable, supporting a seamless shopping experience in multiple languages.Technical Requirements:Framework: The app should be built using Remix, a modern React framework, to ensure a robust and scalable application architecture.UI Components: Utilize Shopify Polaris for designing the user interface, ensuring a consistent look and feel with Shopify's native UI. The design should be adaptable for localization.Data Management: Implement Prisma as the ORM for efficient database management, handling the storage and retrieval of deposit settings and product-deposit associations, with support for storing localized content.Shopify Integration: The application must comply with Shopify's API requirements for public apps, ensuring seamless integration and operation within the Shopify ecosystem.Localization Support: The app should include a framework or library to support internationalization (i18n) and localization (l10n), enabling easy translation of UI texts, messages, and data inputs into various languages.Responsiveness and Compatibility: The app should be fully responsive and compatible with a range of devices and screen sizes, ensuring a seamless user experience across desktop and mobile.Ideal Candidate:Proficiency in React and familiarity with the Remix framework.Experience in developing Shopify apps and working with Shopify's Polaris UI library.Strong background in database management, especially with Prisma ORM.Demonstrated ability to integrate third-party apps with Shopify stores.Expertise in implementing localization and internationalization in web applications.Attention to detail and a commitment to creating a user-friendly and globally accessible interface.Ability to write clean, maintainable, and efficient code.Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.Project Outcome:The successful development of this Shopify Public App will significantly simplify the process of managing deposits for products sold in Shopify stores, with the added benefit of full localization support. It will automate the addition and removal of deposit fees in the shopping cart, ensuring accuracy and efficiency in handling these transactions, while providing a valuable tool for Shopify store owners globally, enhancing their ability to manage product deposits effectively and improving the shopping experience for their customers across different languages.How to Apply:Interested candidates should submit a portfolio of relevant work, including any previous Shopify apps or projects that demonstrate experience with React, Remix, Shopify Polaris, Prisma, and especially localization or internationalization implementations. Please include a brief overview of your approach to the project, highlighting how you plan to tackle the localization requirements, along with any initial thoughts or questions you may have.

title: Advanced Barcode Scanning and Inventory Integration System Development Rasberry Pi / Arduino
description:
### Project Description:We are in search of a highly skilled developer or development team to create an advanced hardware and software solution, taking inspiration from Google's Pointy device but with enhanced compatibility and ease-of-use features. The goal is to enable retailers to seamlessly scan their in-store product barcodes using a Raspberry Pi or Arduino-based system. This system must then transmit the product data to a specified endpoint. The solution will be intricately integrated with our platform, https://www.caleffionline.it, facilitating retailers to list their products as part of a broader marketplace. Furthermore, this system will support online sales by generating a product feed through initial inventory synchronization.#### Key Features and Requirements:1. **Versatile Hardware Compatibility**: The hardware setup, utilizing Raspberry Pi or Arduino, must be adaptable to work with a wide range of barcode scanners, supporting various connection types (USB, serial, etc.). It should accommodate connections via both Ethernet and WiFi to ensure flexibility in different retail environments.2. **Intuitive Software Development**: Develop sophisticated software that not only reads and processes barcode data efficiently but also offers easy configuration options. The software should send processed data to a designated endpoint along with the retailer's store ID, and be capable of initial inventory alignment for creating an online sales-ready product feed.3. **Seamless Platform Integration**: The system should integrate flawlessly with [www.caleffionline.it](https://www.caleffionline.it), allowing for straightforward product listing and management by retailers. This includes automatic updates to the product listings on the platform based on the inventory scans.4. **User-Friendly Interface and Setup**: Emphasize creating a user-friendly interface for the initial setup and ongoing use. Retailers should find it straightforward to connect their hardware to both the internet (via Ethernet or WiFi) and our platform, with minimal technical assistance.5. **Simplified Product Insertion**: Enable retailers to easily add their products to the platform. This should include options for bulk uploads via xls or csv files with field mapping capabilities, or through an automated inventory reading mode using the system itself, making the process as efficient as possible.6. **Security, Privacy, and Documentation**: Implement top-tier security measures to safeguard retailer data and ensure compliance with privacy standards. Additionally, provide comprehensive documentation and support for system setup, use, and troubleshooting, including updates.#### Ideal Candidate(s):
- Demonstrated experience with Raspberry Pi or Arduino, especially in developing compatible systems for diverse hardware interfaces
- Advanced proficiency in software development for hardware interfacing, with a focus on barcode scanners and network connectivity (Ethernet/WiFi)
- A strong track record in web development, particularly with API integrations and creating user-friendly interfaces
- Knowledge and experience with inventory management systems and bulk data handling, including xls/csv file processing

title: Mixpanel Expert
description: Imagine our store is like a big digital warehouse, similar to those quick delivery services like Amazon, Getir, Gorillas, and JOKR, where customers use an app to order what they need, and we deliver it super fast. To make sure we always have what people want without ending up with piles of things nobody buys, we use data—lots of it.Data helps us predict exactly what to stock up on. We do this by keeping track of everything happening on our app. For that, we use a tool called Mixpanel, which is like putting tiny sensors all over the app. These sensors tell us:* What products people are looking at by recording every time someone clicks on an item.* How popular each product is by counting the clicks and how often they're added or removed from shopping carts.* Where each product is popular, so we can map out the best-sellers in every city.* Where our users are, pinpointing the cities they come from.* When our app gets the most action, like the busiest times for views, cart adds, and clicks.We also want to know our customers as if they're friends. This means for every user, say John, we'll know:* His location, contact details, and what he likes to buy the most.* How much time he spends browsing different categories.* His shopping habits—what days and times he usually buys, how much he spends monthly and in total.* His app activity—how long he spends on the app, when he's most active, and how quickly he makes decisions to add things to his cart and check out.All of this information needs to be easy to understand at a glance, which is why we'll use charts and visuals to display it.

description: I need a Rust-based Soroban smart contracts written. It will do the following:1. A token smart contract that implements this interface: (link removed) - symbol is "XYZ" and has a mint() function2. A pool smart contract that holds a number of XYZ tokens, established when created. A buy() function that allows the XYZ token to be purchased from the pool for testnet USDC and a sell() function for sending XYZ to pool and getting USDC out. The price XYZ is sold or bought is based on a bonding curve (the math for the bonding will be provided, its based on 6 input factors). A container smart contract that allows for one or more pools. The container smart contract is public and pools are created through the container create_pool() function (i.e. container will have a map or vector of pools), buys / sells go thru the container functions supplying a pool id. Access to a pool directly is not allowedA simple web page that integrates Freighter to create a pool or buy/sell from the pool (will have a form like this https://ramm.scifn.com/create-pool )A simulated version of this can be found here: (link removed)Success criteria: Fulfills requirements, able to compile and deploy successfully to Testnet and buy and sell XYZs into one or more poolsReminder: There will be 3 smart contracts 1. Token, 2. Pool 3. Container and reference of USDC on testnet as payment token

title: Advanced RAG Pipeline for Multi-Document Analysis
description: Advanced RAG Pipeline for Multi-Document Analysis1. IntroductionPurpose:The RAG pipeline is designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of multi-document analysis by leveraging advanced retrieval techniques. It aims to improve information extraction, comprehension, and synthesis by using document-specific embeddings and summaries.Scope:This system targets applications in research, content creation, and information retrieval where quick, accurate analysis of document collections is crucial. It is expected to support diverse document types and serve various user groups.2. System OverviewArchitecture:• Document Embedding and Summarization: Each document is represented by a persistent vector (embedding) and a concise summary index, facilitating efficient information extraction, retrieval, latent semantic analysis (LSA) and summarization.• Query Engine: Capable of decomposing complex queries into sub-questions and routing these to the most relevant document(s) indices for tailored retrieval.• User interface: a typical input/output interface that retains previous queries up to some defined number of queries. Ability to start a new topic while storing previous queries and providing front end access to query results (ability to store last 10 queries and results at a minimum).3. Functional RequirementsDocument Retrieval:• Embedding-Based Retrieval: The system must support retrieval based on document embeddings that capture semantic information, ensuring high relevance and high accuracy of the retrieved documents.• Content Analysis and extraction: LLM analyzes and synthesizes information from the referenced documents. It includes citations or references for the retrieved information, providing the user with a reference to a section, tab, URL or other location within the analyzed documents for reference by the user.• Embedding Training and Fine-Tuning: The embedding model will be fine-tuned on specific document collections to ensure that the embeddings are highly relevant and tailored to the context of the documents being analyzed.• Summarization Index: Generate document summary indices, aiding quick overview and analysis.Document Analysis:• Query Decomposition: Query engine will decompose complex queries into manageable sub-questions, ensuring that each is directed to the most relevant document(s) and/or summary indices.• Response Synthesis: Generate responses that are not only relevant to the sub-questions but also coherent when combined to address the original query.• References: The responses should be capable of providing location information (citation, page number, section number or other identifying location information), from the information retrievals to the relevant documents.User Interface:• UI Design and Functionality: The system will feature a simple, intuitive user interface that allows users to easily submit queries, view retrieved documents, and interact with the analysis results. The UI will support:• A clean, minimalistic design for ease of use and navigation.• Interactive elements for submitting queries and viewing results.• Catalog of last 10 queries and responses, viewable in the UI front end (open for discussion based on complexity to implement).4. Deliverables• Source Code of prototype application in python including the functional requirements mentioned in this document.• Interactive prototype of the UI.• Documentation outlining the architecture of the pipeline and approach to training the data.

description: Job Title:Full Stack Developer for Video Log Integration and Visualization SystemJob Description:We are seeking a skilled Full Stack Developer to create a dynamic and interactive video log integration and visualization system. This system will combine video footage, various log files, and data entries from MongoDB into a cohesive web-based UI. All logs will be timestamped.Create a frontend web application that displays video alongside a timeline. The timeline should allow users to zoom in/out (ranging from a broad view of a day/week to as detailed as an hour) and scrub through to see events from the logs corresponding to the video timeline.Implement a color-coded system for different logs in the timeline and provide an interactive element (e.g., checkboxes) to enable/disable the display of specific log types.Ensure the system supports second-level precision for event logging and video playback synchronization.Work with existing web technologies and propose a stack that includes a Python-based backend (Flask/Django) and a modern JavaScript frontend framework (React/Vue.js).Requirements:Proficiency in Python for backend development, with experience in Flask or Django.Strong experience in frontend development using React or Vue.js, including state management, API integration, and dynamic data visualization.Experience with data parsing and processing, particularly with structured log files and timestamped data.Familiarity with MongoDB for database integration and querying.Knowledge of video processing and handling technologies.Ability to implement a user-friendly interface with interactive timeline controls for zooming and scrubbing.Experience in creating responsive and intuitive web applications.Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.Additional Skills (Nice to Have):Experience with Docker for application deployment.Familiarity with video.js or similar libraries for video playback.Knowledge of D3.js or other data visualization libraries for creating dynamic, interactive charts and timelines.Project Deliverables:A fully functional web application that integrates video playback with a dynamic, interactive timeline of events from various logs and MongoDB.Documentation on the system architecture, data flow, and user guide for interacting with the UI.Source code for both backend processing scripts and frontend application.How to Apply:Please submit your proposal including:A brief introduction about yourself and your experience relevant to this project.Examples of similar projects you have completed, especially those involving data visualization and web development.Your proposed technology stack and a high-level approach to tackling this project.Your availability to start and estimated timeline to complete the project.Any questions you have about the title: Typeform development for assessment
description: Hi guys,We are in need of a Typeform whiz to help us.Basically we have a 100 point questionnaire that we use to assess a client. These are broken into 5 different performance areas.Each question has 3 columns a performance column, a priority column and a difficulty column.Performance has a score of 1 - 4Priority has a score of 1 - 5Difficulty has a score of 1 - 10 (also an N/A option if required)So for example:Question 1 - Does the client use a sales systems?Performance : Completeley absent (Score 4)Priority: Critical (Score 5)Difficulty: Extremely Hard (1)The score for this question would be a 20 and the maximum score a person can score is 20 and the minumum would be 1. This is calculated by multiplying the performance by the priority.This is then added up to give a score out of 400 which is then divided by 4 to give a score out of 100 for each area of the business.We then use the difficulty score to as a weighting to so if the person has scored 75 out of a hundred but the difficulty to improve the tasks is a weighting of .3 their actual score is 25.This is a tool we use to help understand how to best serve our clients and also appraise their rate of growth. It is used in combination with a number of very important qualatative variables also.We need to find a more efficient way to score this and would love to use a questionnaire of software that will turn this very manual questionnaire into a tool that we can give our customers.We currently use Typeform but are open to anything really. I know if could be completed in excel but UX is quite important. This is why we like things like survey monkey etc.Help is appreciated.Warm regardsAidan

title: Anova/ Ancova
description: InstructionsAn interventional study was conducted to determine the effects of three treatments (exposure) on a health measurement which is measured on a continuous scale. Let’s assume this was a double-blind randomized study and all participants were equally motivated to comply with the intervention arm to which they were assigned. The health measure was collected from each participant at the start of the trial and at the end of the trial. The study outcome was the difference between the measurements before and after the treatment was given and calculated as [measurement at end] – [measurement at start].Create a poster with appropriate tables, figures, and results.Invent a research question, including the health condition and treatment/intervention.InstructionsDetermine whether there were significant differences among the means of ‘Difference’ across the three treatments. You will use SAS Studio for your ANOVA (and maybe ANCOVA) analyses.The dataset has the following variables:• Difference: (Y), the difference between the health measurement taken at two points, post-treatment and pre-treatment. It is calculated as [post treatment – pre-treatment]. This is your study outcome, or independent, variable.• Factor:â€¯An independent variable (X).• Treatment (or intervention):â€¯Three treatments: A, B, and C. This is your study exposure variable. In ANOVA and ANCOVA, this is your categorical variable.Complete the following tasks:1. Conduct an exploratory analysis of Difference and Factor.2. Conduct an exploratory analysis of Difference and Factor stratified by Treatment.3. Create descriptive tables for the results of steps 1 and 2.Consider your mode of communication and create accordingly.4. Check for assumptions: Equal sample sizes of each group, normal distributions, variances are equal across groups, and check for collinearity of Difference and Factor. Assume samples are independent.5. Determine the best analysis plan for measuring whether the effect of three levels of treatment on the means of Difference differed. Include plots. You should decide whether to include ‘Factor’ as a covariate.6. Create at least one figure using a Graphs task.Consider your mode of communication and create accordingly.7. Execute your analysis plan.8. Create a poster, presentation to communicate the objective, intervention arms, methods, results, and interpretation/application. Include appropriate figures and/or tables.Provide:• Poster slide(s)• SAS output

title: Building Digital Wallets - Under Single Bank Account
description: A ledger system under one bank account involves creating a structured digital framework to manage various virtual wallets within the same bank account.Guidelines:1. Understand Digital Wallets: Digital wallets are virtual systems that store payment information, such as credit/debit card details, cryptocurrencies, or other financial instruments, for online transactions. Each wallet can have its own ledger to track transactions.2. Choose a Platform or Framework: Decide on the platform or framework you'll use to build and manage the digital wallets. This could be a custom software solution, a mobile app development platform, or an existing financial technology (fintech) platform that supports digital wallet creation.3. Design Wallet Structure: Plan how you want your digital wallets to be structured. Determine what types of wallets you need (e.g., one for regular purchases, one for savings, one for investments, etc.) and what currencies or assets each wallet will hold.4. Implement Ledger System: Integrate a ledger system into each digital wallet to track transactions. This ledger should include fields for date, description, transaction type (e.g., deposit, withdrawal, transfer), amount, and running balance.5. Security Measures: Implement robust security measures to protect the digital wallets and their associated ledgers. This may include encryption, multi-factor authentication, biometric authentication, and regular security audits.6. User Interface (UI) Development: Design an intuitive user interface for managing the digital wallets and viewing transaction history. The UI should allow users to easily access and interact with their wallets and ledger information.7. Transaction Processing: Implement functionality to process transactions within the digital wallets securely. This includes features such as adding funds, making payments, transferring funds between wallets, and viewing transaction history.8. Account Integration: Integrate the digital wallet system with the underlying bank account to facilitate transfers between the digital wallets and the bank account. Ensure seamless communication and synchronization of transaction data.9. Testing and Quality Assurance: Thoroughly test the digital wallet system to identify and fix any bugs or issues. Conduct usability testing to ensure the user experience meets expectations.10. Compliance and Regulations: Ensure compliance with relevant financial regulations and security standards, such as Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements, Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regulations, and Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) compliance.11. Launch and Maintenance: Once testing is complete and regulatory requirements are met, launch the digital wallet system. Continuously monitor and maintain the system to address any emerging issues, implement updates, and enhance functionality based on user feedback.By following these guidelines, you can build a digital wallet system with a ledger system under one bank account, providing users with a secure and efficient way to manage their finances digitally.

Seamless Transition: Naturally transition the conversation to mention 3MetaD. Perhaps relate a feature of our project to the ongoing discussion.11. Highlight USPs: Briefly highlight what makes 3MetaD unique. Focus on aspects that resonate with the current Space's topic.12. Invite Engagement: Encourage listeners to follow our Twitter, visit our website, or join our community for more information.### Collaboration & Networking:Build Relationships: Try to build ongoing relationships with influencers and participants who show interest in 3MetaD.Collaborate: If you find potential collaborators, note them down and discuss how you might work together with the 3MetaD team.Document: Copy the Link: Choose the 'Copy link' option. - Avoid adding special effects, sound effects, or music to streamline the editing process. Only basic cuts and CapCut’s auto caption feature!
- Editing for each clip is expected to be completed within a maximum of 15 minutes after the initial setup. (Watching the Loom training will showcase how fast and simple our editing expectations are). If you believe you cannot edit 1 video in 15 minutes, do not apply. With this, 4 videos per hour is the expected output. So being assigned a batch of 5 videos should take 1 hour and 15-20 minutes MAX.Responsibilities:
- Editing: Focus on creating engaging content by efficiently trimming footage and adding subtitling.
- Subtitles and Overlays: Implement engaging, accurate subtitles and overlays.
- File Management: Adhere to the specified Dropbox organization and naming conventions for efficient workflow and tracking.Requirements:
- Experience: Demonstrated past video editing experience, particularly with short-form, engaging content.
- Technical Skills: Proficiency in CapCut and experience with subtitles and overlays.
- Attention to Detail: An eye for detail to make content both engaging and informative.
- Time Management: Efficient work under tight deadlines.Project Details:
- Location: Remote
- Duration: TBD based on the backlog
- Pay Rate: NO MANUAL TIME TRACKING ALLOWED FOR THIS CONTRACT.Interested candidates, please apply with your portfolio and a brief description of your relevant experience. We look forward to collaborating with you on this vital project!

title: Setup a Docker based reverse proxy+WAF+ssl with 3 CMS containers
description:

- Php on each container to be at least 8.0- Bash on every container
- SSH with unique port on the host machine forwarding to each container,- Phpmyadmin on every container,- Files from each container's www directory have to be mapped to a host machine folder in order to be preserved in the case of rebuilding the container. - here I have a little dejavu with the cross-contamination of my current setup, so if not a good idea to pup files from different sites close to eachother, then we can skip this setup and I'll think of a regular file backup
- This would be nice as well: http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_limit_req_module.htmlIf you have any suggestions to better the idea explained in the beginning - please do so.I may have asked stupid stuff above as I am new to how Docker works and what can or can not be done... so please feel free to correct me so the job requirement becomes more clear. I just want to have a working set of web servers in separate container behind reverse proxy+WAF+ssl to avoid breaching or cross-contamination in the event of a breach.I hope all this makes sense.I really need to hear your thought on this first. I highly doubt that I managed to cover all aspects of what needs to be done to achieve a semi-secure web server setup with my limited skills.Thanks

title: RADIUS Proxy server in multi realm environment
description: We are looking for someone to assist with setting up a RADIUS proxy server. We currently operate a large number of BNGs (NAS devices) which all need to authenticate RADIUS/PPP requests to RADIUS servers. The number of realms being matched is increasing, as well as the number of NAS devices. It is not feasible to keep updating NAS devices on each radius server.For each @realm.tld RADIUS request, the BNG will look up the respective realm, and then query that specific RADIUS server for AAA information (Mikrotik PPPOE Authentication). The RADIUS server will return: IP Address and Up/Down Rate limit. NAS device will send usage/uptime stats to RADIUS server periodically.We require a RADIUS Proxy server, based on FreeRADIUS. This proxy server will now handle the @realm.tld lookup and request AAA from the respective RADIUS server. Our NAS devices will send all radius requests to this Proxy server, which will in turn query the respective RADIUS server, and return Authentication, IP and usage information as required.We will provide two Linx (any flavour) servers, with public IP addresses. A working RADIUS proxy server that proxies requests based on @realm.tld (proxy realms) needs to be configured. Our multiple BNGs (NAS devices) will send all RADIUS requests to either of these two Proxy RADIUS servers, the NAS IP will need to be re-written to match the Proxy, and the request sent to the respective RADIUS. Responses will need to be sent to the correct NAS, and AAA/PPPOE connections established.Possible betterment/additional scope: Including a GUI to manage realms (basically write to proxy.conf file) as well as RADIUS servers and NAS devices.

For instance, if you look for New York, NY on a map using this: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/place-id The pin will drop in downtown Manhattan and a large radius of hotels would include places like New Jersey and Brooklyn... which is not New York. It would also exclude midtown below central park, which is where many people stay. If I am, say, searching for hotels in that area, business travelers generally do not want to be across a river. They want to be in the heart of where they are traveling.For this project, I need someone to get the "business district" center as a lat/long and the radius for a circle that encapsulates 100% of that district... and that circle should be as small and as tight as possible. This should be represented in the google sheet.For some places, this will be very easy and straightforward (like Atlanta, GA). For others (like New York, NY, or Tokyo Japan), you're going to have to be creative and use your judgement as if you were booking business travel for some CEOs and Board members.For now, this is a one-time project but I can see this project expanding to the top 2000 cities in the world, and it will be need to be continuously updated. In the future, we will build sophisticated bounding boxes and polygons that better represent where business travelers might want to travel, but for now, a center point and radius is where we will start.Some images are attached to show you what I mean around searching for New York vs where one might want to stay.
